The repo is a pnpm workspace with one reference **result** and a UI kit
([ADR 0032](../decisions/0032-api-ui-greeting-and-contract.md)):

- A result is a pair of packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`. The reference

The root configs own every gate and reach each package by glob, so a new result
joins every gate with no config entry of its own.

The reference implementation is the **greeting feature**: a name goes in, the
api greets it back. Copy its shape for every new feature.

```

├── web/                                 # @repo/web, Vite + React
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.tsx                     # composition root: DOM, styles, ApiProvider

│   │   ├── index.css
│   │   ├── api-client/                  # the only door to the api
│   │   │   ├── trpc.ts                  # useTrpc, TrpcProvider, RouterInputs, RouterOutputs
│   │   │   ├── ApiProvider.tsx          # real tRPC client over /trpc + QueryClient
│   │   │   ├── TestApiProvider.tsx      # the same providers over typed in-memory handlers
│   │   │   ├── testApiHandlers.ts       # TestApiHandlers, one handler per procedure path
│   │   │   ├── useTestApiClients.ts
│   │   │   └── index.ts                 # public surface
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   │   └── greeting/                # one folder per route, kebab-case
│   │   │       ├── GreetingPage.tsx     # the page: composes the route's components
│   │   │       ├── GreetingForm.tsx     # one component per file
│   │   │       ├── GreetingMessage.tsx
│   │   │       ├── PageHeader.tsx        # this route owns its header
│   │   │       ├── useGreeting.ts       # server state + local state
│   │   │       ├── useGreetingForm.ts   # form state

│   │   │       ├── *.test.ts(x)         # co-located tests

│   │   └── features/<feature-name>/     # optional: shared by multiple routes

    │   ├── router.ts                    # appRouter and the AppRouter type
    │   ├── trpc.ts                      # initTRPC: router, procedure, createCallerFactory
    │   └── features/

    │           ├── index.ts             # public surface: greetingRouter
    │           ├── procedures.ts        # validates input, delegates to application
    │           ├── application.ts       # use cases: greet
    │           ├── domain.ts            # pure types and rules: Greeting, formatGreeting
    │           ├── integrations.ts      # storage and every effect (the greeting has none)
    │           └── *.test.ts
    ├── etc/

│   ├── Button.tsx
│   ├── TextField.tsx

```

## Roles

[`.fallowrc.jsonc`](../../.fallowrc.jsonc) is the one rules file. Each role is
a Fallow zone, and its patterns match every result through the brace glob
`{apps,showcase/*}`. Fallow fails any value import the table does not allow,
and `coverage.requireAllFiles` fails any source file that sits in no role. A
role may import types (`import type`, `export type … from`) from any other
role ([ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)).
Inline `type` specifiers count too, as in `import { type Greeting }`, when
every specifier carries one. Fallow reads a plain `import { Greeting }` as a
value import even when the file uses `Greeting` only as a type, so write
`import type`.
A slice of a role still imports nothing from a sibling slice. Paths below are
relative to a result root (`apps/` or `showcase/<id>/`).

| Role | Files | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web-app` | `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`, `web/src/index.css` | `web-routes`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-api-client` | `web/src/api-client/**` | no other role |
| `web-routes` | `web/src/routes/<route>/**` | `web-features`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-features` | `web/src/features/<feature>/**` | `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `ui` | `packages/ui/src/**` | no other role |
| `api-app` | `api/src/server.ts`, `api/src/router.ts` | `api-trpc`, `api-procedures` |
| `api-trpc` | `api/src/trpc.ts` | no other role |
| `api-procedures` | `api/src/features/<name>/{index,procedures}.ts`, `features/<name>/procedures/**` | `api-trpc`, `api-application` |
| `api-application` | `api/src/features/<name>/application.ts`, `features/<name>/application/**` | `api-domain`, `api-integrations` |
| `api-domain` | `api/src/features/<name>/domain.ts`, `features/<name>/domain/**` | no other role |
| `api-integrations` | `api/src/features/<name>/integrations.ts`, `features/<name>/integrations/**` | `api-domain` types only |

Tests (`*.test.ts(x)`), `web/e2e/**`, `web/index.html`, `web/vite.config.ts`
and `etc/**` sit outside the roles. A file that grows too large becomes a
folder of the same name, such as `features/<name>/application/`, and keeps its
role.

The canonical diagram [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd)
shows every role and every value direction the rules allow. Each result has
its own generated diagram,
[`apps/architecture.mmd`](../../apps/architecture.mmd) for the reference and
`showcase/<id>/architecture.mmd` for a trial, with the role edges its imports
resolve to. An edge is dashed where the contract allows its pair for types
only. A type-only import along a direction that also allows values draws
solid, because Fallow's graph records no import kind; the trial comparison
reads the sources and counts that edge as type-only. Both come from
`pnpm arch:diagram`, with the same node names.

## Result structure

`tooling/architecture/structure.mjs` checks every result alike, the reference
included ([ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-result-diagrams-and-structure-validation.md)):

- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no
  role.
- A result with one production route slice keeps its web feature code in that route.
  `single-route-features` rejects `web/src/features/**` and
  `web/etc/features-*.api.md`, including orphan reports. Only production
  source establishes another route
  ([ADR 0055](../decisions/0055-single-route-code-stays-in-its-route.md)).
- In each api feature with application and domain source files, application
  imports or re-exports at least one value from that feature's domain.
  `application-without-domain-rule` checks Fallow's resolved edges and the
  shared import-kind reader in `tooling/architecture/imports.mjs`.
- Each result's scaffold API reports, `web/etc/api-client.api.md` and
  `api/etc/api.api.md`, keep the reference's exported names and kinds
  (`scaffold-exports`). The api-client barrel keeps `ApiProvider`,
  `RouterInputs`, `RouterOutputs`, `TestApiHandlers`, `TestApiProvider` and
  `useTrpc`. Fallow exempts only the two router type re-exports from unused
  export findings; the structure check makes them mandatory
  ([ADR 0054](../decisions/0054-domain-rules-in-application-and-a-fixed-api-client-surface.md)).
- A result root holds `web/`, `api/` and `architecture.mmd`. A web package
  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
  rather than link it.
- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
  lists only external ones.
- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
  pragma.

## The api file roles

| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing by value: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. It imports domain types only; application calls domain rules and integrations. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |

The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:

```ts
// apps/api/src/router.ts
import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
import { router } from './trpc.ts';

export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
```

Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
because Vite resolves it.

## The web state model

| State | Owner | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema)), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
mutation or form of its own.

Any web role may name an api type with `import type` from `@repo/api`. The api
client is the only web module that wires the tRPC client and imports its
packages, `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query`. Everything else
reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:

```ts
// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
const trpc = useTrpc();
const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));

// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const mutation = useMutation(
  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
  }),
);
```

Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:

```tsx
function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
  const view = render(
    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
      <GreetingPage />
    </TestApiProvider>,
  );
  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
}
```

A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.

## The rules (and why)

Each rule fails a check on a seeded violation in a committed test
(`tooling/architecture/boundaries.test.ts`, `scripts/eslint-policy.test.ts`,
`tooling/architecture/typescript.test.ts`, `tooling/architecture/structure.test.ts`).
The check's message names the fix.

| Rule | Why | Enforced by | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routes own page composition. | One place per page keeps navigation readable. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
| A single-route result keeps web feature code in its route and removes unused feature reports. | One page has no cross-route sharing boundary. | Structure `single-route-features` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Sibling slices stand alone: a route imports no other route, a feature no other feature. | Each slice changes without breaking its siblings. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` for every result; Fallow child zones for the `apps/web` routes | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Every file belongs to one role and one slice. | Extra layers and loose files hide structure. | Fallow `coverage.requireAllFiles`; `policy/slice-isolation` for a loose file under `src/routes/` or `src/features/` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm lint:policy` |
| A package reaches another only by its package name. | Public exports are the only contract. | `policy/slice-isolation` (relative import out of the package) | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| A module is imported through its `index.ts`. | The public surface is a deliberate, reviewed list. | ESLint `no-restricted-imports`; API reports | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm api:check` |
| Procedures validate their input with Effect Schema. | Data from the network is untrusted until parsed. | ESLint `policy/procedure-input-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |

## Architecture checks

`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
file:

- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
  differs from a fresh run.
- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.

`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
included.

## Showcase results

A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.

- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
  nothing from another result.
- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.
- Its structure, public API, dependencies, component boundaries and
  conventions are compared with every other run, failed runs included, in
  `docs/trials/comparison.md`, which `node tooling/trial/compare.mjs`
  generates ([ADR 0035](../decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md)). Keep each
  difference inside a spec freedom that ADR or
  [ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)
  lists: a type-only import between roles, and dropping a re-export a gate
  flagged, are among them.

## What this template intentionally omits

The template leaves out a router library, a store, a database and auth. They
are stack choices, not agentic principles. A result keeps its data in memory
inside `integrations.ts`. When you add one of them, record the choice as an ADR
in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.

## How to extend

Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.

### Add an api feature

1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
   storage or any effect.
2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.

### Add a procedure

1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
   `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`.
2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
   delegate to one application function.
3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
   `procedures.test.ts`.

### Add a route

1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
   `index.ts` that exports the page.
2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
   runs every spec in that folder.

### Add a web feature

Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
import it through its `index.ts`. A result with one production route slice
keeps that code inside `routes/<route>/` and removes its old feature barrel
and API report. The structure gate counts distinct route slices containing
production source; it rejects feature paths and feature reports when that
count is one. For multiple routes, review still establishes actual reuse.

### Finish

1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.

132	
133	- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
134	  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
135	  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no

138	  `single-route-features` rejects `web/src/features/**` and
139	  `web/etc/features-*.api.md`, including orphan reports. Only production

154	  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
155	  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
156	  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
157	  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
158	  rather than link it.
159	- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
160	  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
161	  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
162	  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
163	  lists only external ones.
164	- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
165	- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
166	- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
167	  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
168	  pragma.

170	## The api file roles
171	
172	| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
173	| --- | --- | --- |
174	| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
175	| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
176	| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing by value: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
177	| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. It imports domain types only; application calls domain rules and integrations. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
178	| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |
179	
180	The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:
181	
182	```ts
183	// apps/api/src/router.ts
184	import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
185	import { router } from './trpc.ts';
186	
187	export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
188	export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
189	```
190	
191	Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
192	the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
193	with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
194	because Vite resolves it.

196	## The web state model
197	
198	| State | Owner | Where |
199	| --- | --- | --- |
200	| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
201	| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema)), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
202	| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |
203	
204	A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
205	mutation or form of its own.
206	
207	Any web role may name an api type with `import type` from `@repo/api`. The api
208	client is the only web module that wires the tRPC client and imports its
209	packages, `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query`. Everything else
210	reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:
211	
212	```ts
213	// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
214	const trpc = useTrpc();
215	const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));
216	
217	// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
218	const queryClient = useQueryClient();
219	const mutation = useMutation(
220	  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
221	    onSuccess: () =>
222	      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
223	  }),
224	);
225	```
226	
227	Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
228	per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
229	hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:
230	
231	```tsx
232	function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
233	  const view = render(
234	    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
235	      <GreetingPage />
236	    </TestApiProvider>,
237	  );
238	  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
239	}
240	```
241	
242	A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
243	`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.

245	## The rules (and why)
246	
247	Each rule fails a check on a seeded violation in a committed test
248	(`tooling/architecture/boundaries.test.ts`, `scripts/eslint-policy.test.ts`,
249	`tooling/architecture/typescript.test.ts`, `tooling/architecture/structure.test.ts`).
250	The check's message names the fix.
251	
252	| Rule | Why | Enforced by | Proved by |
253	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
254	| Routes own page composition. | One place per page keeps navigation readable. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
255	| A single-route result keeps web feature code in its route and removes unused feature reports. | One page has no cross-route sharing boundary. | Structure `single-route-features` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
256	| Sibling slices stand alone: a route imports no other route, a feature no other feature. | Each slice changes without breaking its siblings. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` for every result; Fallow child zones for the `apps/web` routes | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
257	| Every file belongs to one role and one slice. | Extra layers and loose files hide structure. | Fallow `coverage.requireAllFiles`; `policy/slice-isolation` for a loose file under `src/routes/` or `src/features/` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm lint:policy` |
258	| A package reaches another only by its package name. | Public exports are the only contract. | `policy/slice-isolation` (relative import out of the package) | `pnpm lint:policy` |
259	| A module is imported through its `index.ts`. | The public surface is a deliberate, reviewed list. | ESLint `no-restricted-imports`; API reports | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm api:check` |
260	| Procedures validate their input with Effect Schema. | Data from the network is untrusted until parsed. | ESLint `policy/procedure-input-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
261	| Procedures delegate to application logic. | Transport stays thin; logic stays testable. | Fallow `api-procedures` value-imports only `api-trpc`, `api-application` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
262	| Integrations import domain types only. | Storage can change independently of domain rules. | Fallow `api-integrations` allows `api-domain` through `allowTypeOnly` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
263	| Each feature's application imports or re-exports a value from its domain. | Domain rules have one place in the use case's dependency chain. | Structure `application-without-domain-rule` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
264	| Scaffold API exports match the reference's names and kinds. | Every result exposes the same api-client and api-app surface. | Structure `scaffold-exports`; API report freshness | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm api:check` |
265	| The domain is pure, and application knows no tRPC. | Rules test as plain functions. | Fallow `api-domain`; `contract/domain-pure`, `contract/application-without-trpc`; `tsconfig.domain.json` (no Node types) | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit`, `pnpm typecheck` |
266	| Effects run only in integrations or the api composition root. | One place to swap storage or IO. | `contract/effects-in-integrations`, `contract/io-effects-in-integrations`, `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
267	| The web reaches the api only by type: `import type` of the router type. | The bundle carries no server code. | Fallow `allowTypeOnly` (a value import of `api-app` fails); the `types`-only export of `@repo/api`; `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client`, `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
268	| UI primitives hold no business logic. | The kit stays reusable across results. | Fallow `ui` imports nothing by value; `contract/ui-without-logic` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
269	| One React component per file. | One file, one reason to change. | ESLint `policy/one-component-per-file` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
270	| State, server state and form state live in `use*` hooks. | Components render; hooks wire. | ESLint `policy/state-and-effects-in-hooks` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
271	| Forms validate with Effect Schema. | One schema language across web and api. | ESLint `policy/form-uses-effect-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
272	| Web code has the DOM and no Node; api code has no DOM and only erasable syntax; domain code has neither. | The browser has no Node, and Node strips types and runs the source as is. | `tsconfig.json` (web, ui), `tsconfig.api.json` and `tsconfig.domain.json` over `tsconfig.base.json` | `pnpm typecheck` |
273	| Behaviour is defined by each result's E2E specs. | The product contract survives refactors. | Playwright, one project per result | `pnpm e2e` |

285	## Architecture checks
286	
287	`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
288	file:
289	
290	- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
291	  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
292	  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
293	- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
294	  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
295	  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
296	  differs from a fresh run.
297	- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
298	  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
299	  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
300	  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
301	  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
302	  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.
303	
304	`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
305	point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
306	with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones

309	## Showcase results
310	
311	A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
312	([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
313	harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
314	lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.
315	
316	- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
317	  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
318	- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
319	  nothing from another result.
320	- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
321	  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
322	- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
323	  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
324	- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
325	  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.
326	- Its structure, public API, dependencies, component boundaries and
327	  conventions are compared with every other run, failed runs included, in
328	  `docs/trials/comparison.md`, which `node tooling/trial/compare.mjs`
329	  generates ([ADR 0035](../decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md)). Keep each
330	  difference inside a spec freedom that ADR or
331	  [ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)
332	  lists: a type-only import between roles, and dropping a re-export a gate
333	  flagged, are among them.

342	## How to extend
343	
344	Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
345	reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.
346	
347	### Add an api feature
348	
349	1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
350	   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
351	   storage or any effect.
352	2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
353	   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
354	   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
355	3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
356	   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.
357	
358	### Add a procedure
359	
360	1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
361	   `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`.
362	2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
363	   delegate to one application function.
364	3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
365	   `procedures.test.ts`.
366	
367	### Add a route
368	
369	1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
370	   `index.ts` that exports the page.
371	2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
372	   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
373	   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
374	3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
375	4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
376	5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
377	   runs every spec in that folder.
378	
379	### Add a web feature
380	
381	Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
382	is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
383	import it through its `index.ts`. A result with one production route slice
384	keeps that code inside `routes/<route>/` and removes its old feature barrel
385	and API report. The structure gate counts distinct route slices containing
386	production source; it rejects feature paths and feature reports when that
387	count is one. For multiple routes, review still establishes actual reuse.
388	
389	### Finish
390	
391	1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
392	2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
393	   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
394	3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.

446	## Contract rules
447	
448	The Fallow rule pack
449	[`tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc`](../../tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc)
450	reports each finding as `policy-violation` `contract/<id>`, an error. Tests are
451	outside every rule.
452	
453	| Rule id | What it keeps |
454	| --- | --- |
455	| `contract/domain-pure` | `domain.ts` imports no `@trpc/server`, no `effect` and no Node module. `tsconfig.domain.json` also gives it no Node globals. |
456	| `contract/application-without-trpc` | `application.ts` imports no `@trpc/server`; procedures map errors to tRPC. |
457	| `contract/effects-in-integrations` | `fetch`, `self.fetch`, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync` and `Effect.runFork` run only in `integrations.ts` or the api `server.ts` and `router.ts`. |
458	| `contract/io-effects-in-integrations` | Network, storage, process and shell work runs only there too. |
459	| `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | Node IO modules (`fs`, `http`, `net`, `child_process`) are imported only there too. |
460	| `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client` | `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query` are imported only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
461	| `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | Web and ui code imports `@trpc/server` only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
462	| `contract/ui-without-logic` | `packages/ui` imports no query, form, schema or tRPC library. |
463	
464	## State ownership
465	
466	| State | Owner | File |
467	| --- | --- | --- |
468	| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` from the api client, with `queryOptions` or `mutationOptions` | `use<Name>.ts` in the route folder (`useGreeting.ts`) |
469	| Form state | React Hook Form with `standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))` and `defaultValues` | `use<Name>Form.ts` (`useGreetingForm.ts`) |
470	| Form schema | Effect Schema | `<name>FormSchema.ts` (`greetingFormSchema.ts`) |
471	| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |
472	
473	After a mutation, refresh the queries it changes in `onSuccess` with
474	`queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() })`.
475	
476	## Api file roles
477	
478	| File | Holds |
479	| --- | --- |
480	| `features/<name>/procedures.ts` | The feature router. Validates each input with `Schema.toStandardSchemaV1` and delegates to application. |
481	| `features/<name>/application.ts` | Use cases. Calls domain and integrations; knows no transport. |
482	| `features/<name>/domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. |
483	| `features/<name>/integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect. |
484	| `features/<name>/index.ts` | The public surface: the feature router. |
485	
486	See [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full role table and the
487	greeting reference.
488	
489	## Judgment calls
490	
491	- **Full words in identifiers.** Write `name` and `request`. The name is the
492	  cheapest documentation an agent has. Established acronyms such as E2E, CI,
493	  ADR, UI, IO, and URL are fine.
494	- **Hooks wire state, components render, pure functions hold logic.** See
495	  [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).
496	- **Build with `@repo/ui` primitives.** Use `Button` and `TextField` for
497	  controls, and add a primitive to `packages/ui` when a result needs a new one.
498	- **Validate data at an IO boundary.** Parse network, storage, and environment
499	  data before trusting its type, as `server.ts` decodes `PORT` with Effect
500	  Schema. A type assertion is a claim, and validation is proof.
501	- **Fail loudly at boundaries.** `main.tsx` throws when `#root` is missing.
502	
503	## Enforced commit and branch conventions
504	
505	| Convention | Enforced by |
506	| --- | --- |
507	| Commits use Conventional Commits, `type(scope): subject`, lower case with no trailing period. | commitlint on `commit-msg` |
508	| PR titles use Conventional Commits. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
509	| Branches are `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`, for example `feat/greeting-trim-name`. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
510	| A new dependency arrives with a new ADR that names it. | `pnpm check:adr` in `pnpm verify` and CI |
511	
512	## Commit judgment
513	
514	- Write the subject in the imperative mood.
515	- Keep one logical change per commit, so the diff stays reviewable.

# Architecture

> This is the anchor for **showcase #2**: agent-written code must follow the
> patterns described here. When asked to verify or review work, an agent checks
> the change against this document first.

## The shape

The repo is a pnpm workspace with one reference **result** and a UI kit
([ADR 0032](../decisions/0032-api-ui-greeting-and-contract.md)):

- A result is a pair of packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`. The reference
  result lives in `apps/` (`@repo/web`, `@repo/api`). Each generated trial
  result lives in `showcase/<id>/` with the same shape.
- `packages/ui` (`@repo/ui`) holds the UI primitives every result renders with.
- `tooling/results.mjs` (`listResults`) is the one place that discovers
  results: the reference first, then each `showcase/<id>` that has both
  `web/package.json` and `api/package.json`, sorted by id.

The root configs own every gate and reach each package by glob, so a new result
joins every gate with no config entry of its own.

The reference implementation is the **greeting feature**: a name goes in, the
api greets it back. Copy its shape for every new feature.

```
apps/
├── web/                                 # @repo/web, Vite + React
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.tsx                     # composition root: DOM, styles, ApiProvider
│   │   ├── App.tsx                      # mounts the routes; holds no business logic
│   │   ├── index.css
│   │   ├── api-client/                  # the only door to the api
│   │   │   ├── trpc.ts                  # useTrpc, TrpcProvider, RouterInputs, RouterOutputs
│   │   │   ├── ApiProvider.tsx          # real tRPC client over /trpc + QueryClient
│   │   │   ├── TestApiProvider.tsx      # the same providers over typed in-memory handlers
│   │   │   ├── testApiHandlers.ts       # TestApiHandlers, one handler per procedure path
│   │   │   ├── useTestApiClients.ts
│   │   │   └── index.ts                 # public surface
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   │   └── greeting/                # one folder per route, kebab-case
│   │   │       ├── GreetingPage.tsx     # the page: composes the route's components
│   │   │       ├── GreetingForm.tsx     # one component per file
│   │   │       ├── GreetingMessage.tsx
│   │   │       ├── PageHeader.tsx        # this route owns its header
│   │   │       ├── useGreeting.ts       # server state + local state
│   │   │       ├── useGreetingForm.ts   # form state
│   │   │       ├── greetingFormSchema.ts  # Effect Schema for the form
│   │   │       ├── *.test.ts(x)         # co-located tests
│   │   │       └── index.ts             # public surface: GreetingPage
│   │   └── features/<feature-name>/     # optional: shared by multiple routes
│   ├── e2e/                             # the behaviour map: greeting.spec.ts, accessibility.spec.ts
│   ├── etc/                             # generated API reports
│   └── vite.config.ts                   # proxies /trpc to API_ORIGIN (default http://127.0.0.1:3001)
└── api/                                 # @repo/api, Node with native type stripping
    ├── src/
    │   ├── server.ts                    # composition root: the HTTP server on PORT (default 3001)
    │   ├── router.ts                    # appRouter and the AppRouter type
    │   ├── trpc.ts                      # initTRPC: router, procedure, createCallerFactory
    │   └── features/
    │       └── greeting/
    │           ├── index.ts             # public surface: greetingRouter
    │           ├── procedures.ts        # validates input, delegates to application
    │           ├── application.ts       # use cases: greet
    │           ├── domain.ts            # pure types and rules: Greeting, formatGreeting
    │           ├── integrations.ts      # storage and every effect (the greeting has none)
    │           └── *.test.ts
    ├── etc/
    └── package.json                     # exports only { ".": { "types": "./src/router.ts" } }
packages/ui/                             # @repo/ui, react as its only peer
├── src/
│   ├── Button.tsx
│   ├── TextField.tsx
│   ├── styles.css                       # imported once in main.tsx as '@repo/ui/styles.css'
│   └── index.ts
└── etc/ui.api.md
showcase/<id>/                           # a Todo trial result: the same shape, scope @<id>
├── architecture.mmd                     # generated by pnpm arch:diagram
├── web/                                 # @<id>/web: package.json, index.html, vite.config.ts, src/, e2e/, etc/
└── api/                                 # @<id>/api: package.json, src/, etc/
```

## Roles

[`.fallowrc.jsonc`](../../.fallowrc.jsonc) is the one rules file. Each role is
a Fallow zone, and its patterns match every result through the brace glob
`{apps,showcase/*}`. Fallow fails any value import the table does not allow,
and `coverage.requireAllFiles` fails any source file that sits in no role. A
role may import types (`import type`, `export type … from`) from any other
role ([ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)).
Inline `type` specifiers count too, as in `import { type Greeting }`, when
every specifier carries one. Fallow reads a plain `import { Greeting }` as a
value import even when the file uses `Greeting` only as a type, so write
`import type`.
A slice of a role still imports nothing from a sibling slice. Paths below are
relative to a result root (`apps/` or `showcase/<id>/`).

| Role | Files | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web-app` | `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`, `web/src/index.css` | `web-routes`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-api-client` | `web/src/api-client/**` | no other role |
| `web-routes` | `web/src/routes/<route>/**` | `web-features`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-features` | `web/src/features/<feature>/**` | `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `ui` | `packages/ui/src/**` | no other role |
| `api-app` | `api/src/server.ts`, `api/src/router.ts` | `api-trpc`, `api-procedures` |
| `api-trpc` | `api/src/trpc.ts` | no other role |
| `api-procedures` | `api/src/features/<name>/{index,procedures}.ts`, `features/<name>/procedures/**` | `api-trpc`, `api-application` |
| `api-application` | `api/src/features/<name>/application.ts`, `features/<name>/application/**` | `api-domain`, `api-integrations` |
| `api-domain` | `api/src/features/<name>/domain.ts`, `features/<name>/domain/**` | no other role |
| `api-integrations` | `api/src/features/<name>/integrations.ts`, `features/<name>/integrations/**` | `api-domain` types only |

Tests (`*.test.ts(x)`), `web/e2e/**`, `web/index.html`, `web/vite.config.ts`
and `etc/**` sit outside the roles. A file that grows too large becomes a
folder of the same name, such as `features/<name>/application/`, and keeps its
role.

The canonical diagram [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd)
shows every role and every value direction the rules allow. Each result has
its own generated diagram,
[`apps/architecture.mmd`](../../apps/architecture.mmd) for the reference and
`showcase/<id>/architecture.mmd` for a trial, with the role edges its imports
resolve to. An edge is dashed where the contract allows its pair for types
only. A type-only import along a direction that also allows values draws
solid, because Fallow's graph records no import kind; the trial comparison
reads the sources and counts that edge as type-only. Both come from
`pnpm arch:diagram`, with the same node names.

## Result structure

`tooling/architecture/structure.mjs` checks every result alike, the reference
included ([ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-result-diagrams-and-structure-validation.md)):

- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no
  role.
- A result with one production route slice keeps its web feature code in that route.
  `single-route-features` rejects `web/src/features/**` and
  `web/etc/features-*.api.md`, including orphan reports. Only production
  source establishes another route
  ([ADR 0055](../decisions/0055-single-route-code-stays-in-its-route.md)).
- In each api feature with application and domain source files, application
  imports or re-exports at least one value from that feature's domain.
  `application-without-domain-rule` checks Fallow's resolved edges and the
  shared import-kind reader in `tooling/architecture/imports.mjs`.
- Each result's scaffold API reports, `web/etc/api-client.api.md` and
  `api/etc/api.api.md`, keep the reference's exported names and kinds
  (`scaffold-exports`). The api-client barrel keeps `ApiProvider`,
  `RouterInputs`, `RouterOutputs`, `TestApiHandlers`, `TestApiProvider` and
  `useTrpc`. Fallow exempts only the two router type re-exports from unused
  export findings; the structure check makes them mandatory
  ([ADR 0054](../decisions/0054-domain-rules-in-application-and-a-fixed-api-client-surface.md)).
- A result root holds `web/`, `api/` and `architecture.mmd`. A web package
  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
  rather than link it.
- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
  lists only external ones.
- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
  pragma.

## The api file roles

| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing by value: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. It imports domain types only; application calls domain rules and integrations. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |

The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:

```ts
// apps/api/src/router.ts
import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
import { router } from './trpc.ts';

export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
```

Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
because Vite resolves it.

## The web state model

| State | Owner | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema)), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
mutation or form of its own.

Any web role may name an api type with `import type` from `@repo/api`. The api
client is the only web module that wires the tRPC client and imports its
packages, `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query`. Everything else
reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:

```ts
// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
const trpc = useTrpc();
const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));

// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const mutation = useMutation(
  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
  }),
);
```

Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:

```tsx
function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
  const view = render(
    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
      <GreetingPage />
    </TestApiProvider>,
  );
  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
}
```

A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.

## The rules (and why)

Each rule fails a check on a seeded violation in a committed test
(`tooling/architecture/boundaries.test.ts`, `scripts/eslint-policy.test.ts`,
`tooling/architecture/typescript.test.ts`, `tooling/architecture/structure.test.ts`).
The check's message names the fix.

| Rule | Why | Enforced by | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routes own page composition. | One place per page keeps navigation readable. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
| A single-route result keeps web feature code in its route and removes unused feature reports. | One page has no cross-route sharing boundary. | Structure `single-route-features` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Sibling slices stand alone: a route imports no other route, a feature no other feature. | Each slice changes without breaking its siblings. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` for every result; Fallow child zones for the `apps/web` routes | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Every file belongs to one role and one slice. | Extra layers and loose files hide structure. | Fallow `coverage.requireAllFiles`; `policy/slice-isolation` for a loose file under `src/routes/` or `src/features/` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm lint:policy` |
| A package reaches another only by its package name. | Public exports are the only contract. | `policy/slice-isolation` (relative import out of the package) | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| A module is imported through its `index.ts`. | The public surface is a deliberate, reviewed list. | ESLint `no-restricted-imports`; API reports | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm api:check` |
| Procedures validate their input with Effect Schema. | Data from the network is untrusted until parsed. | ESLint `policy/procedure-input-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| Procedures delegate to application logic. | Transport stays thin; logic stays testable. | Fallow `api-procedures` value-imports only `api-trpc`, `api-application` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Integrations import domain types only. | Storage can change independently of domain rules. | Fallow `api-integrations` allows `api-domain` through `allowTypeOnly` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
| Each feature's application imports or re-exports a value from its domain. | Domain rules have one place in the use case's dependency chain. | Structure `application-without-domain-rule` | `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Scaffold API exports match the reference's names and kinds. | Every result exposes the same api-client and api-app surface. | Structure `scaffold-exports`; API report freshness | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm api:check` |
| The domain is pure, and application knows no tRPC. | Rules test as plain functions. | Fallow `api-domain`; `contract/domain-pure`, `contract/application-without-trpc`; `tsconfig.domain.json` (no Node types) | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit`, `pnpm typecheck` |
| Effects run only in integrations or the api composition root. | One place to swap storage or IO. | `contract/effects-in-integrations`, `contract/io-effects-in-integrations`, `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
| The web reaches the api only by type: `import type` of the router type. | The bundle carries no server code. | Fallow `allowTypeOnly` (a value import of `api-app` fails); the `types`-only export of `@repo/api`; `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client`, `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
| UI primitives hold no business logic. | The kit stays reusable across results. | Fallow `ui` imports nothing by value; `contract/ui-without-logic` | `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit` |
| One React component per file. | One file, one reason to change. | ESLint `policy/one-component-per-file` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| State, server state and form state live in `use*` hooks. | Components render; hooks wire. | ESLint `policy/state-and-effects-in-hooks` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| Forms validate with Effect Schema. | One schema language across web and api. | ESLint `policy/form-uses-effect-schema` | `pnpm lint:policy` |
| Web code has the DOM and no Node; api code has no DOM and only erasable syntax; domain code has neither. | The browser has no Node, and Node strips types and runs the source as is. | `tsconfig.json` (web, ui), `tsconfig.api.json` and `tsconfig.domain.json` over `tsconfig.base.json` | `pnpm typecheck` |
| Behaviour is defined by each result's E2E specs. | The product contract survives refactors. | Playwright, one project per result | `pnpm e2e` |

`contract/<id>` is a rule in
[`tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc`](../../tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc),
which Fallow loads as a rule pack and reports as an error. The behaviour map
is each result's `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, for example
[`apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`](../../apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts); see
[ADR 0003](../decisions/0003-behaviour-mapped-with-e2e.md). Each feature's PRD
in `docs/prd/`, such as [`docs/prd/greeting.md`](../../docs/prd/greeting.md),
states its intent and links each behaviour to the test that proves it
([ADR 0045](../decisions/0045-prds-state-intent-and-link-their-specs.md)).

## Architecture checks

`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
file:

- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
  differs from a fresh run.
- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.

`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
included.

## Showcase results

A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.

- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
  nothing from another result.
- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.
- Its structure, public API, dependencies, component boundaries and
  conventions are compared with every other run, failed runs included, in
  `docs/trials/comparison.md`, which `node tooling/trial/compare.mjs`
  generates ([ADR 0035](../decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md)). Keep each
  difference inside a spec freedom that ADR or
  [ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)
  lists: a type-only import between roles, and dropping a re-export a gate
  flagged, are among them.

## What this template intentionally omits

in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.

- **Hooks wire state, components render, pure functions hold logic.** See

- **Build with `@repo/ui` primitives.** Use `Button` and `TextField` for
  controls, and add a primitive to `packages/ui` when a result needs a new one.

  data before trusting its type, as `server.ts` decodes `PORT` with Effect

- **Fail loudly at boundaries.** `main.tsx` throws when `#root` is missing.

I built the Todo result in `showcase/todo-01/`, and both gates pass: `pnpm verify` exits 0 and `pnpm e2e` passes all 23 tests, including the 7 fixed acceptance tests. The work is uncommitted. The only changes outside `showcase/todo-01/` are the lockfile entries `pnpm install` added for the two new packages.

**Api (`@todo-01/api`)**
- A `todos` feature with the same layout as the greeting feature:
  - **Domain:** the todo type with only `id`, `title` and `completed`, and the rules to create a todo and flip it.
  - **Storage:** an in-memory `Map` that lives in the api process.
  - **Use cases:** list, add, toggle and delete.
  - **tRPC procedures:** `list`, `add`, `toggle` and `delete`. Each input is checked with Effect Schema, so a blank title is rejected as a bad request. Toggling or deleting an id that doesn't exist returns "not found".
- `server.ts` and `trpc.ts` are copied unchanged from the reference.

**Web (`@todo-01/web`)**
- One page under `routes/todos/`:
  - **Server state:** `useTodos` loads the list through TanStack Query and tRPC. It reloads the list after every successful add, toggle or delete.
  - **Form:** `useTodoForm` uses React Hook Form with the Effect Schema resolver. A blank title shows the "Enter a title" alert and sends nothing to the api.
  - **Components:** each one is in its own file and built from the `@repo/ui` Button and TextField. The checkbox is a plain HTML input, which the conventions allow.
- The api-client files are copied from the reference. Only the router import and the two api-client tests changed, to point at the todos procedures.
- Both `package.json` files match the reference apart from the name and the api dependency.

- Unit tests cover the domain, storage, use cases, procedures, router, form schema, page and api client. Every todo-01 file reaches 100% coverage.
- The result's own Playwright specs are `web/e2e/todos.spec.ts` and `web/e2e/accessibility.spec.ts`.
- I generated the API reports with `pnpm api:report` and the diagram with `pnpm arch:diagram`; `showcase/todo-01/architecture.mmd` is kept.

**Choices you might not expect**
- Toggling sends only the todo's id and the api flips its state, rather than the page sending the new value.
- If loading or saving fails, the page shows an alert: "Could not load the todos" or "Could not save the change".

The prompt points to `.agents/README.md` for the state and form rules, but that file doesn't exist in this clone. I followed `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `CONVENTIONS.md` instead.
